issues.description: Constructor of class Animal: the problem statement UML declares a constructor Animal(String, int) and attributes 'name' and 'age', but the solution implementation defines only Animal(String) and a single 'name' attribute. This mismatch leaves students unsure whether to implement Animal(String, int) with an 'age' field or Animal(String) with only 'name', and may cause tests or provided solution code to diverge from the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either (A) update the UML and problem text to specify Animal(String) with only a 'name' attribute (and adjust any references), or (B) modify the template and solution to add an 'age' attribute and implement a constructor Animal(String, int) plus appropriate getters/setters. Ensure the UML, template repository, and solution repository all use the same constructor signature and attribute set so students know which constructor to implement.

issues.description: The conceptual 'Animal' data model is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML and text declare an 'age' attribute and a two-argument constructor Animal(String, int), while both the template and the solution implement Animal with only a 'name' field and a single-argument constructor Animal(String). Specifically, the UML lists an attribute 'age: int' and a constructor '+ Animal(String, int)' but the provided implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java defines only private String name and public Animal(String name). This mismatch means a student following the problem text would expect to create or call a two-argument constructor and implement getAge()/setAge(int), but the codebase and examples (Main.java instantiations) use single-argument constructors. That inconsistency prevents a straightforward mapping from the requirement to the template/solution and will confuse or block students (e.g., whether to implement an age field, which constructors subclasses should call, and how to update example instantiations).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor and attributes consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix aligning with the UML: update the code to add a private int age field to Animal, add public int getAge() and public void setAge(int), change the Animal constructor to public Animal(String name, int age) and update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to accept and pass the age to super(...). Also update example instantiations in Main.java to use two arguments (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", 3)). Alternatively, if the intent is to keep the simpler single-argument API, update the problem statement/UML to remove the 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructor, and adjust the UML constructor to Animal(String name) and the textual requirements to match.
